verdict_word: Smaller loss than feared in its off-season quarter; full-year guide reaffirmed
takeaways: First report since Vylor, the seed business, split from Corteva. Q3 is the seed off-season, so a loss is normal.
Pro forma net sales were $938 million, down 1%; volume fell 9% while price/mix rose 6% on licensing income and pricing, per the company release.
Soybean sales fell 26% to $133 million on the shift to a licensing model in Brazil; corn rose 4% to $607 million.
The Fly compared organic sales of $911 million with a $918.1 million consensus (a slight miss), so the revenue verdict depends on which number you use.
Full-year guidance reaffirmed: about $2.8 billion adjusted operating EBITDA and $2.25-$2.35 operating EPS. A $3 billion buyback and $0.13 dividend were announced Oct 22.
verdict: Vylor's first report card came in the quarter when seed companies basically sell nothing, and it still lost less than expected. Its old roommate Corteva got the bad Brazil news; Vylor got to say 'reaffirmed.'
